messages:
sara (docs): Hey — spotted a mismatch between the chat streaming docs and the Node SSE example. The docs show `max_tokens` but runtime expects `max_new_tokens` for incremental streams.

matt (sdk): Oh yeah? Where exactly? Can you paste the snippets?

sara (docs): In docs/reference/chat-streaming.md we have this curl and node example:

```
// node SSE example (current doc)
fetch('/v1/chat/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', max_tokens: 256 })
})
```

But the server ignores `max_tokens` for streaming and uses `max_new_tokens` internally, so the example is misleading.

ravi (api): Confirmed on the runtime side: legacy CLI used `max_tokens` in blocking calls; streaming flow was migrated to `max_new_tokens` to avoid double-counting context tokens. We added a compatibility layer but it's flaky for SSE.

julia (pm): Does this affect existing clients? Any user-facing break?

ravi (api): Most clients are fine because we still accept `max_tokens` in non-streaming endpoints. SSE + `max_tokens` sometimes gets ignored -> users might think streaming truncated earlier/later than expected.

sara (docs): Proposed doc changes: update request param name in streaming examples to `max_new_tokens`, add a short note in the param table: "For streaming endpoints, use `max_new_tokens` to control generated tokens; `max_tokens` applies to non-streaming calls." Also update Node SSE snippet and add minimal migration note.

matt (sdk): I'll update the Node snippet in the SDK examples too. Want to include both fields for backward compatibility? e.g. support both in example like: `{ max_new_tokens: 256 /* preferred for stream */ , max_tokens: 9999 /* legacy non-stream */ }`

sara (docs): Hmm prefer we show the preferred usage first and then a one-line compatibility tip below. Keep examples minimal.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 by matt (sdk) — runs: docs lint, linkcheck.

matt (sdk): PR includes: updated docs/reference/chat-streaming.md node & curl snippets, added migration note under "Breaking changes/Notes", and small test in examples/ that validates `max_new_tokens` label appears.

julia (pm): Can we also add a short compat table in the API ref? One row: streaming endpoints -> `max_new_tokens` (preferred), non-streaming -> `max_tokens` (legacy).

sara (docs): Good idea. I'll add that row.

ravi (api): Also please add an implementation note for runtime: when both provided, prefer `max_new_tokens` and ignore `max_tokens` for streaming flows. That makes behavior deterministic.

sara (docs): Added to PR description.

matt (sdk): Link to PR preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/789/reference/chat-streaming.html

sara (docs): Quick checklist before merge: 1) update node snippet in docs 2) update curl examples 3) add compat table row 4) add migration note and server behavior note 5) run linkcheck and examples lint.

julia (pm): Who will merge? Any risk to release notes?

matt (sdk): I can merge after CI passes. We should add a short blurb in the next weekly release notes under "Docs clarifications".

sara (docs): I'll draft release-note blurb after merge.

ravi (api): FYI ops: no infra change needed. Runtime already prefers `max_new_tokens` for streaming but the doc fix avoids confusion.

matt (sdk): CI green ✅. One tiny markdown nit flagged by linter; pushing a fix now.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #789.

matt (sdk): Merged. Closing follow-ups: @sara can you post the release-note blurb and @julia can you confirm the PM note?

sara (docs): Will post blurb in #announcements later today. Draft: "Docs: clarified streaming vs non-streaming token params — use `max_new_tokens` for stream endpoints; `max_tokens` remains for non-streamed calls. See docs PR #789."

julia (pm): Looks good. Thanks all. :tada:

sara (docs): Closing thread — thanks for the quick turnaround!
